Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for last week's demo. Our engineering and finance teams are reviewing the pilot billing and hit a couple of edge cases we want to clarify before we sign the PO. Two specific asks: 

1) Proration when a single inference spans slabs: if a single request produces 18k tokens and our committed slab boundaries are at 10k/20k, how does Redwood prorate the charge? Do you round up to the next slab, split across slabs, or apply a blended per-token rate? Our previous provider rounded each request up to the slab which produced large tail charges.

2) Commit tethering and ephemeral KV prefix reuse: in the pilot we reuse an ephemeral prefix across many short sessions (KV hit rate ~40%). Do you bill the raw generated tokens, or is there any amortization against the committed capacity? In other words, if the KV cache avoids 30% of decode work, can that be reflected as reduced billable tokens or a credit?

Attached is a sample invoice excerpt and a couple of example request traces (timestamps redacted). Can your team provide a short worked example we can show to procurement?

Goal is to finalize the 6-month pilot commitment this week if these are aligned.

Thanks,

On Oct 14, 2028, Jordan Lee wrote:
> Thanks again for last week's demo...

Jordan — thanks for the concrete examples. Below is the short, finance-friendly worked example plus policy notes. I've attached a CSV with the same calculations if you want to plug in alternate volumes (proration-matrix.csv).

Worked example (commit customer, monthly invoice window):
- Commit: 1M tokens/month at $0.0012/token (committed rate)
- Overage slab structure (for ad hoc bursts): 0-10k @ $0.0016, 10k-20k @ $0.0014, >20k @ $0.0011 (per-request slab pricing used only in on-demand accounts)

Scenario A (single 18k-token request on a committed account)
- Approach we apply: blended treatment. The platform charges the committed per-token rate for billable tokens up to the committed volume, then any overage tokens are billed at the committed overage rate. We do not split a single request across multiple ad-hoc slabs for committed customers.
- Example: if you have 995k tokens already used in the month and then submit an 18k request: 5k will be covered by the remainder of the commit (billed at $0.0012), and the remaining 13k is billed as overage at your committed overage rate (typically $0.0014).
- Net: (5k * $0.0012) + (13k * $0.0014) = $6.00 + $18.20 = $24.20 for that request.

Scenario B (no commit, pure on-demand)
- For on-demand customers we do per-request slabing: a single request is mapped to the slab buckets in our public price table (so a single 18k request would be split across 0-10k and 10k-20k at the listed slab rates). That is the behavior that creates the large tail you mentioned.

KV amortization / prefix reuse
- Short answer: KV cache hit-rate is an optimization inside the serving runtime and is not directly billed as "fewer tokens." Billable tokens are a function of decoded/generated tokens plus defined input token accounting. However, we recognize amortization is important for pilots:
  - For committed customers: we can apply an experiential credit policy for pilot periods to reflect measured KV savings. Typically we offer a pilot credit equal to a fraction of the measured CPU decode savings (not a token-for-token reduction) — this is done as a line-item credit negotiated upfront.
  - For long-term contracts: we can bake KV/quantization uplift into the committed rate during negotiation (e.g., lower per-token committed rate tied to expected KV reuse metrics).

Policy caveats
- We do not silently round every single request up to the next slab for committed customers.
- Extremely large single-request outliers (>100k tokens) may be subject to additional price review and could be treated as a separate "batch" pricing case; we'll flag these to sales if a customer consistently issues such requests.

Jordan — I attached proration-matrix.csv with the line-by-line math. If that looks good, Ben can approve a pilot credit and we can add a short clause to the SOW that defines the pilot credit calculation (measured KV hit-rate * agreed multiplier).
